# Third-party attribution

Algorithm 939: Amparo Gil, Javier Segura and Nico M. Temme, 2014, ACM TOMS 40(3), Article 20, DOI 10.1145/2591004. Original source: https://calgo.acm.org/939.zip. The unchanged archive, extracted source, upstream documentation and original notice (939.head) are retained in algorithm939/. The applicable ACM source notices remain in force.

GammaCHI: Amparo Gil, Javier Segura and Nico M. Temme. The selected Fortran sources and original README from the GammaCHI distribution used in the CDF experiment are retained in gammachi/. No new license is assigned to them.

Python and C++ component ports, seed adapters, and exposed fixed-count Fortran variants derive from these works. They are identified in source docstrings and build substitution records. Claims about source equivalence do not imply bitwise identity across special-function libraries.

Project paper: Zhong-Xuan Mao and Jing-Feng Tian, "Efficient numerical computation
of the generalized Marcum Q-function with applications", arXiv:2611.29209 (2026),
https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.29209. This project citation does not replace upstream
attribution or license terms. See ../docs/licensing.md for the licensing review.

The bundled GammaCHI source identifies the 2021 version. Its official software
record lists GPLv2: https://data.mendeley.com/datasets/d2kwwvsyny/1 . The earlier
2015 program summary listed Standard CPC licensing; the two releases must not
be treated as having interchangeable license terms.
